subject: PrimeStream: Latency tipping point — model v4.3 traffic shift & escalation
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@primestream.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-22T08:12:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden p95 jump on model v4.3 after scheduled traffic shift

Diego —

Raising an urgent alert from our on-call after the traffic shift you performed at 07:45 PT. We observed a sharp p95 jump for inference calls routed to model v4.3: baseline ~220ms -> current ~840ms (see attached snapshot). Error rates are stable but user-facing latency is causing timeouts in our frontend and some sessions are being dropped.

We believe the change from v4.2 -> v4.3 variant might have introduced a kernel path that spikes under the request distribution (many short prompts with streaming). Can you confirm whether any runtime kernel changes or quantization profiles were activated in the rollout? PrimeStream is seeing customer-impacting degradation and asked us to escalate.

Attachments: traffic-snapshot-20271122.csv

— Evan
Evan Brooks
Head of Platform Engineering, PrimeStream

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@primestream.com>
Date: 2027-11-22T08:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump on model v4.3 after scheduled traffic shift

Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks for the flag, Evan. I pulled the live traces and the CANARY rollout to v4.3 completed at 07:50 PT for PrimeStream (traffic pin to variant v4.3). Initial indicators:
- p95 rose sharply starting at 07:47 and stabilized at elevated levels by 07:52.
- Memory/KV pressure is within expected range; CPU kernel-time for attention ops increased by ~2.8x on the serving nodes handling short-prefix traffic.
- We did enable a new fused-attention kernel and an experimental int8-quant profile for v4.3 to reduce cost in long-sequence workloads; this may be suboptimal for short streaming bursts.

Immediate asks:
1) Approve temporary traffic soft-cap (30% reduction) back to v4.2-compatible variant while we confirm kernel impact.
2) Permit us to enable an emergency fallback policy for PrimeStream to route to v4.2 (read-only) for 60 minutes while we gather traces and a regression patch.

Evan, can you confirm tolerance for a short traffic cap and whether your SREs are comfortable with client-side short retry windows while we act?

I'll attach p95_trends and open a Grafana snapshot for the team.

— Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@primestream.com>
Date: 2027-11-22T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump on model v4.3 after scheduled traffic shift

Team —

Iauthorize a provisional rollback gate for PrimeStream under our emergency playbook. Proposed steps:
- Approve traffic soft-cap: reduce traffic to v4.3 by 40% immediately; re-route to v4.2-compatible variant (no model weights change, just variant selection).
- Activate emergency fallback switch for PrimeStream for up to 90 minutes or until we validate a regression patch.
- Exempt this incident from standard SLA breach credit calculation provided we: 1) notify PrimeStream GTO and 2) agree a remediation window (they accept a 4-hour root-cause ETA).

Ben, please coordinate infra-side pinning and confirm the impact on pooled Dedicated customers. Marissa, can you draft a short customer note (1-2 lines) to Evan confirming timeline and the temporary nature of the cap?

Evan — we need your explicit OK for the traffic cap and the fallback activation. If you authorize, we will implement within 10 minutes and monitor p95; if p95 improves we will keep traffic at the soft-cap while we ship a targeted kernel fallback.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@primestream.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-22T09:11:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump on model v4.3 after scheduled traffic shift

Thanks — PrimeStream accepts the traffic soft-cap and the fallback activation. Two notes:
1) We need the customer-facing note before you touch production (ops needs to coordinate cache warm-up).
2) Werequire a short post-incident confirmation that the temporary SLA exemption will not count as a precedent for future long-window exceptions; weunderstand emergency fixes but want clarity on documentation.

Please proceed.

— Evan

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@primestream.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-22T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 jump on model v4.3 after scheduled traffic shift

Evan —

Short customer-facing note for Ops (please reply if any edits):

PrimeStream team — we observed an unexpected latency increase after a variant rollout that affects a portion of your traffic. We are temporarily capping traffic routed to the new variant and failing over the remainder to the previous variant while we push a targeted remediation. We expect p95 to return to normal within the next 30–60 minutes and will follow up with a detailed incident recap and remediation plan.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
